Band: zero-width: within the pinned scope the hourly list rate is a single exact published number with no variance. Month length (672-744 h), burstable credit surcharges, Savings Plans and Spot are OUT-OF-BAND modifiers, named per row, not band edges.

citations.note: $0.0725/h x 730 = 5293c/month. Cross-checked to the cent against the AWS Price List Bulk API (version 20260904231117).

monthly_cost_per_instance.measured_context: cache.t4g.medium — AWS ElastiCache us-east-1 / On-Demand / Redis engine / standard support / 730 h per month; node-hour only. Band: zero-width at the Redis/Memcached standard-support rate. The Valkey engine is CHEAPER and Extended Support is DEARER; both are different products/support states, not a price range for this row, so they are named here rather than used as band edges.

db.t4g.medium — AWS RDS PostgreSQL us-east-1 / On-Demand / Single-AZ (band high = Multi-AZ) / 730 h per month; INSTANCE-HOURS ONLY (excludes storage, provisioned IOPS and backup above the free allocation). Band: deployment spread: low = Single-AZ, high = Multi-AZ. Both are on-demand, standard-tier, us-east-1 PostgreSQL, so the band is fully in scope. Multi-AZ is ~2x Single-AZ.

citations.note: $0.065/h Single-AZ x 730 = 4745c/month. MySQL/MariaDB run ~3.9% cheaper than PostgreSQL for the same class.

assumptions.subject: workload
assumptions.statement: 1,200 req/s at peak across a company's agent fleet: 70% tool calls, 18% tool discovery, 9% OAuth token exchange, 3% batched audit flushes.

assumptions.subject: architecture
assumptions.statement: The MODEL is not in this design. A tool gateway brokers MCP tool traffic; the model runs in whatever agent host is calling it. There is therefore no token spend here - the cost is fleet compute and audit retention.

assumptions.subject: gw
assumptions.statement: 900 req/s per gateway instance: OAuth token validation, tenant policy evaluation and JSON-Schema validation of every tool argument on 2 vCPU.

assumptions.subject: upstream
assumptions.statement: 150 tool executions/s per upstream MCP server instance - the tools do real work (database queries, third-party APIs) at roughly 35 ms each. The gateway is cheap; the fleet behind it is what you pay for and what saturates first.

assumptions.subject: cache
assumptions.statement: Every request checks the cache. 8% of tool calls miss the routing/policy entry, 5% of discovery calls miss the manifest, and 40% of token exchanges must read the registry (short-lived tokens).

assumptions.subject: audit
assumptions.statement: One immutable audit record per tool call and per token exchange, about 1.5 KB, kept for 12 months. Flushes to the archive are batched roughly 25:1, which is why the flush flow carries a much smaller share than the event rate.

assumptions.subject: cost
assumptions.statement: Object-store REQUEST charges are not priced: the engine has a single request rate calibrated to API-gateway requests, and applying it to S3 PUT/GET would be the wrong rate. Only per-GB archive storage is billed here.

assumptions.subject: cost
assumptions.statement: Egress is billed per response: ~8 KB per tool result, ~32 KB per full tool manifest, ~512 B per token exchange. Traffic to upstream MCP servers stays inside the network and is not billed as internet egress.

assumptions.subject: db
assumptions.statement: The write primary is a SINGLE instance and the engine reports it as a single point of failure. That is the shape of the design: high availability comes from Multi-AZ standby failover, which v1 cannot express - `instances` means active capacity, and a warm standby serves no traffic. Budget for it (the RDS price band tops out at Multi-AZ) and treat the SPOF flag as a reminder, not a modelling error.

assumptions.subject: engine
assumptions.statement: Per-tenant isolation, per-tenant rate limits and noisy-neighbour effects are NOT modelled - v1 simulates one aggregate stream. A gateway that holds at 1,200 rps in aggregate can still fail a single tenant.

_library.summary: Org-wide gateway in front of many MCP servers: OAuth, per-tenant policy, quotas and an immutable audit trail of every tool call.
